fixes.explanation: Olive trees do show up in Zechariah's visions, but not here. In Zechariah 4:3 he sees two olive trees beside a lampstand. This time, what comes out from between the two mountains is "four chariots," and the mountains are made of bronze. Easy to mix up, friend, because the man sees a LOT of things.
Yes, baker. The text says the horses were red, black, white and dappled, "…all of them strong." Not one weak team in the bunch. That's a lineup I'd be proud to have in my bakery.

The text doesn't say Zechariah chases anything, friend. It says he inquired of the angel who was speaking with him: "What are these, my lord?" (Zechariah 6:4). He asks what they are. Chasing four chariots on foot sounds like a great way to get very tired and learn very little.

Shinar does show up in Zechariah's earlier vision, friend. In Zechariah 5:11 he hears that a house will be built for the woman in the basket in the land of Shinar. But here the angel says the four spirits go forth "…from their station before the Lord of all the earth." That's a very different address.

North belongs to the black horses, not the dappled ones. The angel says, "The one with the black horses is going toward the land of the north…" The dappled horses head "…toward the south." Easy to swap them, baker, since they're all in the same sentence.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, "…those going to the land of the north have given rest to My Spirit in the land of the north." He's the one speaking, so it's His Spirit.
